newsitem.title: TURKEY: Three Turkish Islamist MPs face charges.
newsitem.headline: Three Turkish Islamist MPs face charges.

text.p: Turkey's secularist government is trying to lift the parliamentary immunities of three Islamist MPs so they can be taken to court for alleged incitement and embezzlement, Anatolian news agency said on Monday.
It said the Justice Ministry had prepared two written requests demanding the national assembly strip the deputies' protection from prosecution.

One of the documents, sent to the parliamentary speaker's office, outlines a charge against Islamist deputy Sevki Yilmaz of "inciting the people to break the law" in a series of public addresses. Anatolian said the other document accuses him of insulting the secularist armed forces in a 1993 speech.

Yilmaz resigned from the Islam-based Welfare Party last month after Turkish television channels showed videos of him apparently insulting fellow MPs and criticising Turkey's secular system at public meetings.
Yilmaz says the tapes, some from the early 1990s, were tampered with to alter his remarks.

Anatolian said former Welfare MP Ibrahim Halil Celik was accused in a Justice Ministry document of promoting "enmity between the people" for remarks quoted in a newspaper in which he was reported to have said blood would flow if the army hindered the Islamists.
A current Welfare deputy, Lutfi Yalman, faces charges of embezzling money collected to help Moslems in Bosnia, the agency said.

Turkey's secularist establishment has started legal investigations into members of the previous Islamist-led government since former prime minister Necmettin Erbakan resigned last month under pressure from the secularist army.
